data.narrative:
Atmos Space Cargo is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company that has raised €30M to date. Valuation triangulation draws on a comparables universe of 13 firms spanning both public equities (5 tickers including RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and private peers (8 firms including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs).

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression proved applicable. The peer-median approach could not be deployed due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum sample thresholds—while 11 same-sector peers exist, none yielded three or more datapoints in relevant narrow filters. Public-comp anchoring was precluded by the absence of disclosed revenue for the target, a typical constraint on private company valuations. The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the €30M raised proxy, implying a Series A exit or next-round valuation of €60M.

Given reliance on a single method, the valuation range is necessarily compressed. Analysis supports €51M–€69M, centered on €60M. Key uncertainties stem from the narrow methodological foundation: the 2.0x multiplier reflects typical but not universal Series A progression, and the absence of revenue visibility prevents revenue-multiple anchoring to public comparables. Additional disclosure of financial metrics or negotiated transaction data would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
